market_name: Will 1 Fed rate cut happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability move is sustained or a stale-quote blip; cross-check fed funds futures (SOFR/SR3) for confirmation of a real repricing.
time_plan.1h: Compare TLT/IEF move against 2y and 10y yields to confirm duration is responding rather than idiosyncratic ETF flow.
time_plan.2h: Look for a macro catalyst (CPI, jobs, Fed speaker, geopolitical shock) that would justify the repricing; if none, fade the signal.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether the implied-probability move held into the US session and whether rates markets corroborated.
time_plan.12h: Mark realized TLT return vs expectation; note whether the prediction-market move led or lagged the bond move.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of Fed rate cuts in 2026 reflects a dovish shift in policy expectations. Lower expected policy rates pull the front-to-belly of the curve down and, via expectations, lift long-duration bond prices. TLT is the most liquid, broadly-traded proxy for duration. Note that 'at least 1 cut in 2026' is likely already priced near-certain, so incremental information is low unless the market swings toward NO (no cuts / hikes), which would flip the sign.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm the probability move is genuine and directional (more cuts = dovish); check DXY and EURUSD for immediate reaction.
time_plan.1h: Verify move is US-driven, not a foreign-central-bank story pushing the dollar the same direction.
time_plan.2h: Check for competing macro drivers (risk-off flows can strengthen USD even amid cut expectations).
time_plan.6h: Reassess UUP vs 2y yield spread to confirm rate-differential channel.
time_plan.12h: Record realized UUP return vs expectation and whether the FX move tracked the rates move.

predictions.reasoning: A dovish repricing (higher cut probability) narrows US rate differentials versus other currencies, which typically weakens the dollar. UUP is a liquid DXY proxy. The effect is second-order and easily overwhelmed by relative moves at other central banks, so confidence is modest and magnitude small.

evidence_used: Market resolves on FOMC statements / target fed funds rate changes in 2026
'At least 1 cut' is a low strike, likely already carrying high implied probability
Standard transmission: dovish Fed expectations lift duration and weaken USD
Liquid proxies TLT and UUP directly express duration and dollar views
uncertainty_notes: Direction of asset move depends entirely on WHICH way the implied probability shifts; a move toward NO (no cuts/hikes) flips all signs
A 'at least 1 cut' market is likely near-certain and thus low-information at the margin
12h moves of the 700bps tradable threshold are implausible for TLT/UUP, so neither prediction is tradable under the stated bar
Prediction markets are noisy; a probability jump may be a liquidity/stale-quote artifact rather than genuine leakage

llm_justification.summary: This is a US monetary-policy market on whether the Fed cuts at least once in 2026. A sharp dovish repricing (higher cut probability) would map to higher long-duration Treasury prices (TLT up) and a modestly weaker dollar (UUP down) via lower expected policy rates and narrower rate differentials. However, the low strike ('at least 1 cut') is likely already near-certain, incremental information is small, and any realistic 12h move in these liquid proxies falls well below the 700bps tradable threshold. Direction inverts if the market swings toward NO.
key_assumptions: The probability move reflects genuine changes in Fed-cut expectations, not noise
A rise in cut probability equals a dovish shift
Rate-differential and duration channels dominate over risk-sentiment channels in the 12h window
TLT and UUP remain liquid, representative proxies during the window
failure_modes: The market resolution is already effectively priced (near-certain YES), so no leakable signal exists
The probability move reverses within hours as a stale/thin-quote artifact
Risk-off dynamics could strengthen the dollar and lift bonds simultaneously, breaking the UUP thesis
A foreign central bank move could dominate USD direction regardless of Fed expectations
Sign error: an apparent 'dovish' jump could actually be repricing toward fewer cuts, flipping both predictions
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
